messages.content: We settled on Kauai rather than Maui after talking it through. Please compare the three Poipu resorts for October 24 through November 1, eight nights. I want the real totals, not just the room rates. Also check whether arriving Friday instead would materially improve the options.

I’ll price both eight-night patterns: Saturday, October 24 through Sunday, November 1, and the fallback of Friday, October 23 through Saturday, October 31. I’ll include lodging taxes, mandatory resort charges, parking, and any required deposit, then separate breakfast value because it is included at only one property. I’ll also verify the exact room category, spa access, and refundable deadlines.
Good. The three are Grand Hyatt Kauai, Koloa Landing, and Ko’a Kea. For a resort trip like this, keep the customer rating at 4.0 or better; don’t drop below that just to save a few hundred dollars.

All three clear that floor on the same metric: current Google customer ratings are 4.6 for Grand Hyatt Kauai, 4.7 for Koloa Landing, and 4.5 for Ko’a Kea. Those are customer-review ratings, not hotel class ratings. I’m checking flexible rates rather than prepaid offers.
Start with the Saturday dates. Show me exactly how the breakfast and parking affect the comparison.

For October 24-November 1, the Grand Hyatt’s flexible partial-ocean-view king with lanai is $5,000 for eight nights. Estimated lodging and fee taxes are $969.12, and the mandatory resort fee is $440. Self-parking is included, bringing the stay total to $6,409.12. The selected package includes daily breakfast for two, conservatively worth $70 per day or $560 over the stay. After recognizing that value, its comparison cost is $5,849.12. The hotel would charge a $745.14 first-night deposit now; that is part of the total, not an additional fee.
And Koloa Landing? Make sure the less expensive rate is actually cancellable.

Koloa Landing’s flexible deluxe studio king with furnished lanai is $4,520. Taxes and taxable mandatory charges add $883.42, the resort fee totals $400, and self-parking is $280, for $6,083.42 all in. It does not include breakfast. Allowing $60 per day for breakfast for two adds $480, making the practical comparison $6,563.42. The rate is cancellable without penalty through 11:59 p.m. Hawaii time on October 17. A $673.01 first-night deposit is due at booking and remains part of the quoted total.
So despite the lower room rate, it is about $714 more than the Hyatt after breakfast value. What room does Ko’a Kea actually guarantee? I don’t want “ocean view requested.”

Ko’a Kea can confirm an oceanfront king with private lanai; the category name and oceanfront designation would appear on the reservation. Eight nights are $6,040, taxes and taxable charges are $1,153.61, the resort fee is $360, and required valet parking is $320. The complete total is $7,873.61. No breakfast is included. The deposit is $899.20, credited toward the stay. Cancellation is free through 6:00 p.m. Hawaii time on October 10; after that, the deposit becomes nonrefundable.
That is a significant premium. Check the spas before we rule it out. We would want two treatments on Tuesday or Wednesday, preferably late morning, and we do not need a couples room.

Ko’a Kea’s spa can confirm two separate 80-minute treatments at 11:00 a.m. Wednesday, October 28. The estimated treatment total is $760 including the automatic 20% service charge, and it is not included in the room total. Grand Hyatt’s Anara Spa has one 10:30 a.m. opening Tuesday and a second at 1:30 p.m.; it cannot currently place both treatments in the late-morning window. Koloa Landing has two Wednesday openings, but they are at 9:00 a.m. and 2:00 p.m. None of the spa appointments is being held yet.
Now compare Friday arrival. Keep each alternative at eight nights, so October 23 through October 31.

For October 23-31, Grand Hyatt is $6,281.40 all in with the same partial-ocean-view king, included parking, and breakfast for two. That is $127.72 less than the primary dates. Koloa Landing is $5,962.18 including resort fee, tax, and parking, or $121.24 less; the same studio is available. Ko’a Kea rises to $8,028.06 because the oceanfront category is priced higher that Friday, an increase of $154.45. The cancellation terms and deposit structures are unchanged. Friday arrival does not unlock a better room category or better spa timing.
Then keep the Saturday dates. Before deciding, confirm whether the Hyatt room is genuinely ocean-facing and whether the breakfast covers the full menu or only a credit.

The Hyatt category is “Partial Ocean View King with Lanai.” The view is guaranteed only as partial ocean view and may include substantial garden or pool foreground; the hotel will accept a full-ocean-facing request but will not confirm it in that category. Breakfast is a daily $70 credit for two at Ilima Terrace, not unrestricted full-menu inclusion. The credit does not roll over and excludes gratuity. Taxes on eligible breakfast charges are covered within the credit.
And the Koloa room has no defined ocean view at all, correct? Also verify whether any of these fees are payable again at checkout.

Correct. Koloa Landing’s deluxe studio is categorized by room type, not view, and an ocean-facing location would be only a request. For all three quotes, the resort fee and parking figures cover all eight nights and are already included in the stated totals. They may be collected at checkout rather than prepaid, but they are not added a second time. Incidental authorizations are separate temporary holds: approximately $200 per night at Grand Hyatt, $150 per night at Koloa Landing, and $250 per night at Ko’a Kea. Those holds are not trip costs unless charged against.

The Ko’a Kea premium over the Hyatt is $1,464.49 before spa and breakfast outside the Hyatt credit. That is high, but it buys the confirmed oceanfront room and the two treatment times. Are the spa slots cancellable independently?

Yes. Ko’a Kea’s spa appointments can be cancelled without charge until 11:00 a.m. Hawaii time on October 27, 24 hours before treatment. Later cancellation or no-show would be charged in full. The hotel and spa have separate cancellation rules, so cancelling the room would not automatically cancel the treatments.

Book Ko’a Kea for October 24 through November 1 in the confirmed oceanfront king. Use the flexible rate and the card ending 1842. Do not book the spa yet, but note the Wednesday times so we can decide after flights. Please verify the cancellation deadline one final time before submitting.

The final booking screen confirms an oceanfront king with private lanai for two adults, October 24-November 1, at $7,873.61 including estimated taxes, mandatory resort fees, and valet parking. The $899.20 deposit is charged to the card ending 1842 and applies toward that total. Cancellation is permitted without penalty until 6:00 p.m. Hawaii time on October 10; cancelling after that point forfeits the deposit. I’m submitting that flexible reservation now.
Proceed.

Ko’a Kea is confirmed for October 24-November 1 in an oceanfront king with private lanai. The reservation total is $7,873.61, with a $899.20 deposit charged to the card ending 1842 and the remaining estimated balance due at the property. Free cancellation ends at 6:00 p.m. Hawaii time on October 10. The two 11:00 a.m. spa openings for Wednesday, October 28 were documented but not held or booked. The Friday-date fallback is no longer needed, and flights remain unpurchased.
